prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: In frames 1–3, the camera wearer looks straight down at a round green basin filled with grain inside a white sack directly in front and below at roughly 0.4–0.8 m, with both of the wearer's hands within arm's reach at 0.3–0.6 m above and around the basin rim while the surrounding straw-covered ground lies farther below at about 1.0–1.5 m. Across frames 3–5, the wearer lifts the basin closer to the torso and turns and tilts the head upward, revealing two open white grain sacks on the ground to the left at 1.0–1.8 m in frame 4 and a wider outdoor bank beside a body of water in frame 5, where a white bucket sits near the bank about 3–4 m ahead and a second person stands in shallow water in the upper right about 8–12 m away (roughly 5–8 m beyond the bucket), facing left and away from the camera wearer. The depth map clearly separates the foreground basin and upright sack walls from the similarly textured grain and dry straw in frames 1–4—which blend together visually in the RGB image—and isolates the silhouettes of the midrange bucket and distant standing person against the background in frame 5. However, the depth map is unreliable in frame 5 where the foreground sacks and basin at the bottom edge saturate to uniform pure white, losing internal 3D relief, and across the water surface where reflections flatten the depth gradient.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map attempts to parse the foreground objects within arm's reach (0.3–0.8 m directly below the wearer) and the distant person in the upper right of frame 5 (about 8–12 m away, facing left in the water and not looking toward the wearer), tracking the basin as it shifts from the center in frames 1–3 to the lower right in frames 4–5 as the wearer turns rightward and looks up. In frame 5, it isolates the distant standing person in the upper-right water and outlines the top rim of the closest white sack in the lower-left foreground (about 1.0–1.5 m away, partially out of view at the bottom edge), which helps distinguish the distant human figure from the water reflection. However, the map is largely unreliable for semantic identity and boundary precision in this agricultural scene: in frame 1 it merges the wearer's two hands and the grain basin into a single 'person' mask, in frame 2 it misclassifies the background ground and sack as 'person' and the grain basin as 'cake' while only labeling the right hand as 'person', and in frames 3–5 it mislabels the basin, sacks, and a sack rim as 'sandwich', 'cake', and 'bird'. It also completely misses the wearer's left hand in frames 2–3, the wearer's right hand in frame 4, the basin at the bottom right of frame 5, and the midrange bucket on the bank.
descriptions.pose: The pose map renders only isolated magenta 2D hand skeletons for the camera wearer's hands within immediate arm's reach (about 0.3–0.5 m in front of and below the viewpoint) and detects no yellow body skeletons in any frame. In frame 1, it captures the wearer's left hand open and angled up and to the right over the center-left of the basin; in frame 2, it switches to the wearer's right hand in a pinched posture near the lower-right rim; and in frame 4, it detects the right hand gripping the upper-right rim of the lifted basin while the wearer's arms remain mostly out of view below the bottom frame edge. Where detections succeed, the articulated finger keypoints show exact finger flexion and palm orientation that are difficult to resolve against the similarly colored dark grain and shadow in the RGB frames. However, the map is highly incomplete, failing to detect the wearer's right hand in frame 1, the left hand in frames 2 and 3, the right hand in frame 3, all hands in frame 5, and the entire body skeleton of the distant standing person in the upper right of frame 5 (about 8–12 m away).
